label: Inferred Dresser geyserite at three localities
summary: Djokic and colleagues interpret microlaminated siliceous rocks at three Dresser Formation DFc1 localities, approximately 2 km apart, as geyserite.

label: Dresser siliceous ridges interpreted as sinter terracettes
summary: At Dresser locality 1S, the authors interpret convex siliceous ridges above stratiform geyserite as resembling mid- to distal-apron hot-spring sinter terracettes.

sources.title: Earliest signs of life on land preserved in ca. 3.5 Ga hot spring deposits

label: Dresser barite masses interpreted as fossil hot-spring pools
summary: The authors propose that at least some large Dresser barite masses at hydrothermal vein tips are mineralized remnants of terrestrial hot-spring pools and shallow hydrothermal plumbing.

sources.title: Earliest signs of life on land preserved in ca. 3.5 Ga hot spring deposits

label: Inferred gas-bubble preservation in Dresser microbial EPS
summary: The authors interpret roughly 200 µm circular structures in Dresser geyserite as gas bubbles likely trapped in microbial EPS, while leaving thermal-fluid versus metabolic gas origin unresolved.

sources.title: Earliest signs of life on land preserved in ca. 3.5 Ga hot spring deposits

label: Dresser quartz fabric proposed as microbial palisade texture
summary: The authors suggest that bedding-normal quartz crystals in Dresser sinter terracettes are analogous to recrystallized microbial palisade fabric formed by silicified filaments.

sources.title: Earliest signs of life on land preserved in ca. 3.5 Ga hot spring deposits

label: Dresser stromatolitic laminates associated with sinter clasts
summary: At Dresser locality 24S, geyserite rip-up clasts occur among domical and conical stromatolitic laminates; their internal laminae and sediment onlap are described as consistent with microbial origin.

label: Dresser microfossil-like vesicles interpreted as volcanic glass
summary: A 2018 study interprets spheroidal-to-lenticular Dresser microstructures resembling Archean microfossils as silicified and pyritized vesicular volcanic glass based on size, wall ultrastructure and chemistry.

label: Kerogenous carbon associated with Dresser volcanic vesicles
summary: In the studied Dresser volcanic-glass microstructures, organic kerogenous material accompanies altered glass, with some vesicles lined or filled by carbon and organic-rich laminae enveloping multiple vesicles.

label: Isolated volcanic vesicles can imitate microfossils
summary: The Dresser pseudo-fossil study cautions that isolated reworked silicified volcanic vesicles can adsorb carbon and become pyritized, complicating early-life identification; nanoscale wall analysis may be required to exclude biogenicity.

label: Nutrient limitation conditions basalt microbial element release
summary: In laboratory incubations of HSDP2 drill-core basalt with Burkholderia fungorum, release of Fe and other major elements exceeded abiotic controls only for nutrient-depleted rock-sample assays.

label: Synthetic basalt glass stress and Fe(II) track element release
summary: In biotic laboratory colonization assays using synthetic basaltic glasses, dissolved major-element concentrations increased with greater residual stress and Fe(II) content.

label: Biofilm coverage differs across synthetic basalt glass types
summary: The 2018 colonization assays reported dense biofilm on stressed Fe(II)-rich basalt glasses, versus sparse colonization on unstressed Fe(III)-rich glasses.
